checkpoint_scope: Five-source integrated confirmation after two passed saturation challenges. The batch reconnects data-center accounting to user-level withdrawal evidence, utility adaptation, economy-wide competition and disclosure governance. Runtime facts are excluded.

integrated_confirmation_admissions.title: The Water Footprint of Data Centers

whole_text_audit.extent: Complete water-footprint framework, data-center archetypes, direct cooling and electricity-mediated accounting, source factors, results, sensitivity, discussion and limitations reviewed.

verified_extraction.claim_path: The study builds a preliminary data-center water footprint by joining on-site cooling demand to the water embodied in electricity, then varies data-center size, efficiency, climate and generation technology.
verified_extraction.measurement_and_denominator: Reported footprint intensities are per unit of data-center energy under specified archetypes and water-footprint factors; the range is model-derived rather than a facility inventory.
verified_extraction.heterogeneity_and_regime: Cooling configuration, PUE, climate and electricity source widen the result by orders of magnitude, demonstrating why a single generic data-center factor is unstable.
limitations: The analysis is preliminary and relies on archetypes and literature factors.
Global-average electricity water factors suppress plant and watershed variation.
The denominator is energy rather than computing service.
Results are not a current facility-level national estimate.
anti_patterns: Do not quote the modeled range as observed facility performance.
Do not omit indirect electricity water when claiming a footprint boundary includes operations.
Do not compare unlike data-center archetypes without efficiency and climate controls.

whole_text_audit.format: complete open-access publisher HTML and data descriptor
whole_text_audit.extent: Complete nationwide state-data acquisition, user and point definitions, standardization, measurement-method metadata, anomaly flags, coverage comparison, validation and limitations reviewed.

verified_extraction.claim_path: The database harmonizes state-reported user-level withdrawals while preserving source, point of diversion or use, reporting period, measurement method and known anomalies instead of treating all records as uniform observations.
verified_extraction.measurement_and_denominator: Records represent self-supplied withdrawals, not consumptive use and not municipal deliveries; annual and monthly volumes coexist with heterogeneous reporting thresholds and vintages.
verified_extraction.heterogeneity_and_regime: State law, agency practice, privacy, public accessibility and whether data attach to a user or diversion point determine coverage and comparability.
limitations: Eight states and portions of covered states lack shareable user-level data.
Self-supplied records omit water delivered by public suppliers.
Withdrawal volumes combine direct measurements and estimation methods.
Historical vintages and reporting thresholds differ across jurisdictions.
anti_patterns: Do not label withdrawal records as consumption.
Do not infer zero use from an absent public record.
Do not merge point-of-diversion and place-of-use coordinates without provenance.

integrated_confirmation_admissions.title: Evaluating the economic impact of water scarcity in a changing world

whole_text_audit.extent: Complete coupled basin hydrology and global economic model, scarcity-cost definition, multisector adaptation, deeply uncertain scenarios, results, sensitivity, discussion and limitations reviewed.

verified_extraction.claim_path: The study defines economic scarcity impact through the cost of adapting consumption and production when usable water becomes binding, allowing trade and sector substitution to transmit effects beyond the source basin.
verified_extraction.measurement_and_denominator: Economic surplus change is modeled by basin and sector across uncertain futures; physical shortfall is an input, not the economic outcome itself.
verified_extraction.heterogeneity_and_regime: Agriculture, thermal generation and other sectors differ in substitution cost, while trade can relocate both water demand and welfare effects.
limitations: The coupled global model is not a local rate or permit forecast.
Economic structure, trade and adaptation elasticities drive modeled welfare effects.
Basin resolution cannot identify a data-center facility burden.
Scenario outcomes should remain conditional rather than predictive.
anti_patterns: Do not equate physical scarcity volume with economic loss.
Do not analyze a basin-sector shock as economically isolated.
Do not assume every sector can conserve or substitute at the same cost.

integrated_confirmation_admissions.title: The challenge of closing the climate adaptation gap for water supply utilities

whole_text_audit.extent: Complete approximately 5,600-utility drought-risk framework, demand and climate scenarios, adaptation options, benefit-cost and tariff-finance screen, results, sensitivity and limitations reviewed.

verified_extraction.claim_path: The study separates technically cost-effective drought adaptation from the smaller subset that utilities can finance through projected tariff revenue, exposing a bankability gap behind modeled resilience benefits.
verified_extraction.measurement_and_denominator: Risk is unsustainable or disrupted supply by utility under scenario; adaptation benefit and benefit-cost ratio are calculated separately for each option and utility.
verified_extraction.heterogeneity_and_regime: Supply portfolios, storage, demand growth, climate and household revenue bases produce different adaptation choices and financing constraints across utilities.
limitations: Global utility modeling uses standardized abstractions rather than local engineering plans.
Tariff revenue is not the only possible financing source.
Modeled benefit does not establish approval, construction or operation.
Household supply risk does not directly measure industrial service capacity.
anti_patterns: Do not call a technically beneficial adaptation financed.
Do not use regional drought exposure as proof of a utility outage.
Do not treat all utilities as having equal balance-sheet or tariff capacity.

integrated_confirmation_admissions.title: Data Centers Water Footprint: The Need for More Transparency

whole_text_audit.extent: Complete direct, electricity-mediated and supply-chain boundary discussion, facility and corporate disclosure critique, spatial and temporal context, community planning implications and recommendations reviewed.

verified_extraction.claim_path: The commentary organizes data-center water dependence across direct cooling, electricity generation and supply-chain stages, then shows that aggregated voluntary reporting prevents communities and regulators from evaluating local capacity and tradeoffs.
verified_extraction.measurement_and_denominator: Facility withdrawals, consumption, WUE, electricity-mediated water and corporate totals answer different questions and require source, location, time and boundary metadata.
verified_extraction.heterogeneity_and_regime: Cooling technology, climate, water source, grid mix, workload and disclosure boundary determine both physical use and what can be inferred publicly.
limitations: The article is a synthesis and policy commentary, not a new facility census.
Illustrative reported figures retain company and study boundary differences.
Transparency enables evaluation but does not itself reduce use.
Supply-chain water remains especially difficult to allocate.
anti_patterns: Do not compare corporate water totals without aligning organizational and operational boundaries.
Do not call WUE complete water-footprint disclosure.
Do not replace absent facility evidence with national rhetoric.

integrated_atomic_observations.statement: A data-center operational footprint can be dominated by electricity water even when site cooling is the visible use.
Energy-normalized water factors do not normalize computing service or utilization.
Efficiency, cooling, climate and generation mix interact strongly enough to make a generic factor unstable.
An archetype range is model evidence and should not be narrated as an observed fleet distribution.
User-level self-supplied withdrawals exclude both consumptive loss and water delivered by a public supplier.
Measurement method, anomaly status, record vintage and state reporting rules belong in the evidence rank.
A point of diversion and a place of use can occupy different locations and cannot be spatially merged by convenience.
Public-record coverage reflects state law and agency access as well as physical water use.
The same physical water constraint imposes different economic costs on sectors with different substitution options.
Trade transmits water-scarcity effects beyond the basin where the hydrologic constraint originates.
Economic impact requires a behavioral adaptation model rather than a volumetric shortfall multiplier.
Abundant physical water may remain economically unavailable when infrastructure or institutional barriers bind.
A technically cost-effective supply adaptation may remain unavailable when tariffs cannot support its finance.
Modeled risk reduction is not an implementation forecast unless financing, approval and delivery are represented.
Utility adaptation capacity is distributed unevenly through supply portfolios, revenue bases and household affordability.
Demand management, new supply, storage and transfers solve different physical and financial failure modes.
Corporate totals cannot establish facility conditions without site, source, period and organizational-boundary disclosure.
WUE, withdrawals, consumption and full footprint are not interchangeable measures of performance.
Transparency, replenishment and physical demand reduction are distinct actions and outcomes.
Local planning requires peak demand and source-capacity information that annual corporate reporting usually omits.

integration_assessment.rule_evaluation: The integrated batch adds no universal family, preserves all hard boundaries and reconnects facility, grid, watershed, utility, economic and disclosure evidence without contradiction. Source admission is complete.
